concerns.text: SC-002 requires the model to be 'statistically distinguishable from a null model... with p < 0.05'. The spec does not define the null model (e.g., mean predictor, random shuffle) nor the statistical test (e.g., permutation test, t-test) to be used. Without a defined procedure, this criterion is unverifiable.

SC-004 requires a 'permutation importance score > 0.05'. The threshold 0.05 is arbitrary and not derived from a baseline or statistical test defined in the spec. It is unclear if this is an absolute value or a p-value. If absolute, the unit (e.g., RMSE drop) is missing. If p-value, the test is undefined. This makes the success criterion unmeasurable.

Acceptance Scenario 1 for US-3 requires the top feature to have a 'statistically significant importance score (p < 0.05 via permutation test)'. The spec does not specify the number of permutations, the null distribution generation method, or the significance test details. This procedure is not reproducible or verifiable as written.

Acceptance Scenario 1 requires 'no missing values in the critical_cooling_rate or mixing_enthalpy columns'. However, US-1 also states the system must 'filter for entries with reported glass-forming labels or critical cooling rates'. If the source data lacks these, the pipeline might produce 0 rows. The criterion 'no missing values' is trivially true for an empty set, but the intent is likely 'at least N rows with no missing values'. The current phrasing allows a 0-row dataset to pass, which contradicts the 'statistical power' intent of SC-001.
